article.title: NFL EDGE Monday Evening Brief
article.dek: The inactive lists are in, the questionable Chargers are decided, and Week 10 ends tonight with one game — and one card on it.

items.headline: Lead: Inactives are in — Njoku and Perryman play, Eboigbe does not
paragraphs: The waiting is over. The final inactive lists came out about 90 minutes before kickoff, and the five questionable Chargers are decided.
David Njoku and Denzel Perryman are active. The Chargers activated both from injured reserve earlier today, and both suit up tonight. Trey Pipkins III and Kayode Awosika are active too.
The one who does not play is Justin Eboigbe, out with an ankle injury. Ladd McConkey was already out with his back injury, and so are Kendall Williamson, Isas Waxter, Bud Dupree, and Brenen Thompson.

For Baltimore, Adam Randall is active after being listed questionable, and Jaylinn Hawkins is out with a knee injury as expected. Jacoby Brissett starts at quarterback. Kickoff is 8:15 p.m. ET at M&T Bank Stadium.

items.takeaway: Njoku and Perryman are in, Eboigbe is out, and the inactive lists are final — Brissett starts for Baltimore against Herbert.

items.headline: Weather: mostly clear and cold in Baltimore — nothing flagged
paragraphs: Mostly clear skies for kickoff, around 37 degrees, a light 2 mph wind from the northwest, and no rain in the forecast. The weather is not a factor tonight.
items.takeaway: Mostly clear, 37 degrees, light wind, no rain — nothing flagged for tonight.

items.headline: One live card: Hit Rate on Baltimore moneyline — now -225, and the price still matters
paragraphs: Hit Rate is Baltimore moneyline at -225 on DraftKings tonight. That is the pick the app thinks is most likely to win. It is not the value play — its expected value is negative. The app's own tutorial says it plainly: Hit Rate is not Profit Rate.

The price moved your way a little since this morning, from -230 to -225. Say it out loud before you touch it. At -225, every $2.25 you risk wins $1. The app rates this one LOW reliability, and its play-through is -228 — if the price drifts past that, the verdict changes.

Watch the book here. At FanDuel the same moneyline is -230 tonight, which is already past the -228 play-through. Same team, same game, different book, different answer. That is exactly what Check is for: type in your book's price and get a verdict on your number.
Balanced has no play tonight, and Value has no play either. The app found nothing plus-EV on this game. A quiet card is a real answer.
items.takeaway: Hit Rate is Baltimore moneyline -225 at DraftKings — inside its -228 play-through — while FanDuel's -230 is already past it; Balanced and Value are empty tonight.

items.headline: The app still sees tonight's game much closer than the market does
paragraphs: The market has Baltimore -4.5. The app's expected margin is about even — basically a coin flip on the spread. That is roughly four and a half points closer than the market.

Same story on the total. The market number moved to 39.5 today, and the app's projection still sits near 44. That is a big gap, and it is exactly the kind of thing to run through Check: type in your book's total and price, and the app runs it back through the model and the evaluator and gives you a bet or no-bet verdict on your price.
If your book is not DraftKings or FanDuel, the board's numbers are not your numbers. Check is how you get a verdict on yours.
items.takeaway: The app sees the game about even on the spread and projects near 44 points against a 39.5 total — Check your price before you pay it.

items.headline: The quarterbacks check out — Herbert against Brissett, and the board knows it
paragraphs: The app is pricing the right quarterbacks for tonight: Justin Herbert for the Chargers, Jacoby Brissett for the Ravens. Brissett is in because Lamar Jackson is out with a thumb injury and Tyler Huntley is out too.

The inactive lists changed nothing at quarterback, so the board's verdicts stand on the names they were built on. If anything changes late, the old verdict is dead — Check the new number before you bet it.

items.headline: Learn the Game: handle vs. tickets — two different kinds of public
paragraphs: When you read a betting split, you will see two numbers: handle and tickets. Handle is the share of the money. Tickets is the share of the bets. They are not the same thing, and the gap between them is what the Fade looks for.

Here is a clearly labeled hypothetical example. Say 70% of the tickets are on the favorite, but only 40% of the handle is. That means lots of small bets on the favorite and fewer, bigger bets on the underdog. The crowd is on one side and the money is leaning the other way.

That split does not prove anything by itself. One book's numbers are not enough, and the line has to move in a way that backs it up. But when you see tickets and handle pulling in opposite directions, you are looking at the kind of disagreement worth watching — and worth waiting on, because a better price may be coming.
items.takeaway: Handle is the share of the money, tickets is the share of the bets — when they pull in opposite directions, the crowd and the money disagree, and that is what a Fade watches for.

items.headline: The total moved a point — 38.5 to 39.5 — and the board caught it
paragraphs: The one real move today is the total. It was 38.5 this morning at both DraftKings and FanDuel. Tonight it is 39.5 at both books. Pinnacle sits a half point lower at 39.0. The board caught all of it.
The spread did not move: Baltimore is still -4.5 at both books. The moneyline moved a little at DraftKings, -230 to -225, while FanDuel held at -230.

The app still sees the game much closer than the market on the spread — its expected margin is about even, against a -4.5 line. On the total, the app's projection sits near 44, against a market number that just moved to 39.5. The gap narrowed a bit with the move, but it is still a big gap. Run your book's total through Check and get a verdict on your price.
If your book's number is different from the board's, tap Check, type in your line and price, and get a verdict on your number.

items.headline: Tonight's job: nothing left to wait for — bet a good number now
paragraphs: The inactive lists are out. That was the last piece of news worth waiting for today, and it is settled.

So there is nothing left to wait for. If your book has a good number and Check says bet, bet now. A good number tonight beats a hoped-for number at kickoff, because waiting lets the number drift the wrong way too.
One more thing: settlement is manual. The tracker only works if you are honest with yourself — log the losers too, the same way you log the wins.
